findings.title: Hung flusher processes are never killed, so a restart runs two flushers on the same shards
findings.body:
In production, processes come from `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`, which builds `SpawnProcess` objects. In CPython, `SpawnProcess` subclasses `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess`, not `multiprocessing.Process` (that is `context.Process`, a sibling class). So `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is always False here, and `process.kill()` never runs. The old code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally.

When `cause == "hang"` (for example, a stall on Redis or on `future.result()`), `_create_process_for_shards` starts a second process for the same shards. That second process gets the same `healthy_since` and `backpressure_since` Values (lines 116-117), while the stuck one keeps running. Once the stuck one recovers, both processes flush the same queue keys at the same time, and segments are produced twice to buffered-segments before `done_flush_segments` removes them. The old process also keeps writing `healthy_since`, which hides later hangs. Each hang leaks another process, up to MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS.

Fix: check `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess)`, or check `hasattr`-free against `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess`, which matches the type annotation at line 68. `join` (line 346) has the same check, so `terminate()` is never called there either. That part is pre-existing. Also, the new `break` at line 341 skips the terminate for every remaining process once the deadline passes.

findings.title: Per-process buffers multiply the `max-flush-segments` budget and loosen the backpressure threshold
findings.body:
`SpansBuffer.flush_segments` computes `max_segments_per_shard = ceil(max_flush_segments / len(self.assigned_shards))` (src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:382-384). It sets `any_shard_at_limit` when a segment has `>= max_segments_per_shard` entries (buffer.py:411-412).

Before this change, one buffer held all N shards, so each flush cycle was capped at `max-flush-segments` in total. Now each of the P processes owns a buffer with N/P shards. Each process may flush up to `max-flush-segments` per cycle, so the consumer as a whole can flush up to P times that, and the per-shard limit rises from M/N to M·P/N. The backpressure trigger at flusher.py:172 therefore fires later than the option intends.

An operator who sets `--flusher-processes` silently changes what `spans.buffer.max-flush-segments` means. Either divide the option by `num_processes` or document the new meaning.

findings.title: Redis memory info is fetched once per flusher buffer on every submit
findings.body: Every `SpansBuffer` gets the same client from `get_redis_client()` (buffer.py:162-163), and `get_memory_info` calls `iter_cluster_memory_usage(self.client)` (buffer.py:375-376). Looping over `self.buffers` therefore sends the same INFO requests P times on each `submit`, and the ratio comes out the same. One call is enough. The same applies to `record_stored_segments` at line 269-270, although there each buffer at least covers different shards.

findings.title: `time.sleep(0.1)` does nothing because the test patched `time.sleep` to a no-op
findings.body: Line 15 runs `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`, so the call at line 62 returns immediately and gives the flusher thread no time, despite the comment. The test only passes because `step.join()` with no timeout busy-waits until the thread exits. Remove the sleep and comment, or use a non-patched sleep as `test_flusher.py` does.

findings.title: The multi-process restart and health-check path has no test
findings.body: `test_flusher_processes_limit` only checks counts in the shard map. Nothing tests `_ensure_processes_alive` restarting one process out of several, or that flushing works when shards are split across processes. A restart test with real spawn processes would have caught the `isinstance` bug at flusher.py:254.

findings.title: Docstring says the flusher creates one process per shard, but the count is capped
findings.body: The number of processes is `min(max_processes, len(shards))`, and the CLI default is 1 (consumers/__init__.py:434). With the default, all shards share one process.

findings.title: `_create_process_for_shard` has no callers, and the `if not process` guard is dead code
findings.body: Nothing calls `_create_process_for_shard`. At line 222, `if not process: continue` can never skip, because Process and Thread objects are always truthy and the dict only ever holds started processes.

findings.title: Metric tag key is `shards` here but `shard` everywhere else
findings.body: `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` is tagged `shards`, while `produce` and `segment_size_bytes` (lines 185, 195) use `shard`. Values also differ: those carry the comma-joined list, and `flusher_unhealthy` (line 244) carries a single int. Dashboards can't group these metrics consistently.
